chunks: Thaʿlabah ibn Maymūn narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Hilāl, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who marries one born of zinā. He said: “There is no harm. It is only considered disliked out of fear of disgrace. Indeed, the child belongs to the loins, and the woman is only a vessel.”
He said: I said, then what about a man who buys a bondwoman born of zinā and has relations with her? He said: “There is no harm.”

key_terms.الْوَلَدُ: the child or offspring under discussion
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no legal harm or prohibition in the matter
key_terms.لِلصُّلْبِ: belonging to the biological paternal line
key_terms.مَخَافَةَ الْعَارِ: fear of social shame or disgrace
key_terms.وِعَاءٌ: a vessel; the term used in the narration
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: it is considered disliked, without being forbidden

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia fiqh to marry someone born of zinā?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that marriage to, and relations with, a person born of zinā are not prohibited. It notes that such a matter may be regarded as disliked due to social disgrace, not because of legal unlawfulness. The report therefore distinguishes between juridical permissibility and social aversion.
